title: AI-assisted MRI interpretation in suspected prostate cancer
summary:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the prostate is an important part of the diagnostic process when prostate cancer is suspected. It helps to better identify clinically significant tumors and may help avoid unnecessary biopsies. However, interpreting MRI images is time-consuming and depends on the experience of the radiologists performing the analysis.

The “PRO-AI” study investigates whether two CE-certified AI software solutions can support the radiological interpretation of prostate MRI examinations in everyday clinical practice. To this end, a total of approximately 1,600 patients across four study centers will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: standard interpretation without AI support, or interpretation supported by one of two AI systems. The final interpretation in all groups will be performed by qualified radiologists.

The primary objective of the study is to compare the diagnostic accuracy of the different interpretation methods in detecting clinically significant prostate cancers. Additionally, the study will examine, among other things, the duration of the interpretation process, the user-friendliness of the AI systems, acceptance among patients and medical staff, and the quality of the reporting.

The study aims to provide insights into whether AI-assisted methods can standardize and make the diagnosis of prostate tumors more efficient in the future.
conditions: Patients who undergo an MRI of the prostate when prostate cancer is suspected

interventions.name: Image acquisition (prostate MRI) according to standard clinical practice, MRI interpretation supported by CE-certified AI system A, final interpretation performed by radiology professionals
Image acquisition (prostate MRI) according to standard clinical practice, MRI interpretation supported by CE-certified AI system B; final interpretation performed by radiology professionals
Image acquisition (prostate MRI) according to standard clinical practice, MRI interpretation by radiology staff without AI assistance

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants must be patients at one of the participating centers.
Participants must be scheduled for a diagnostic MRI of the prostate.
Participants must be of legal age and capable of giving informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Minors and adults who lack the capacity to consent
Unscheduled patients with emergency indications
Previous diagnosis of prostate cancer
